{"name": "charge-review", "steps": "Inputs: the developer's org or account id, the invoice (id or month), the lines and amounts they mean, request ids if they have them.

1. Identify the account. If you have neither org nor account id, ask_developer for org_id (plus invoice_id/invoice_month and line_items/amounts/request_ids in the same call if not given). lookup_account.
2. Check billing channel, plan and has_signed_contract on the account.
   - Not billed directly by Redwood: search_knowledge for the procedure for that exact channel (cloud marketplace vs reseller are different pages; apply only the one matching billing_channel). Support credits/disputes nothing there; tell the developer who bills them and where refunds/credits/invoices go. Open a case only if the current page says so (e.g. a metering mismatch).
3. get_invoice (map a month to an id from lookup_account's invoice list). Read console_confirmed_duplicates (original_line vs copy_lines, decided by where the usage records point), same_requests_but_unconfirmed, and same_amount_but_different_requests. get_usage for request ids the developer gave.
4. Classify:
   a. Console-confirmed duplicate: act only on the copy line, never the original.
   b. Look-alike (same amount/description, different request ids), no second line, or usage pointing to neither/both lines: NOT a confirmed duplicate. Say so plainly with the console evidence. Never say a credit is likely before the console confirms a duplicate.
   c. Wrong rate/quantity/product, unrecognized usage, retries/cancelled streams, token mismatch: search the usage/token pages; if they explain it, explain and stop.
   d. Waive/reduce a correct charge (goodwill, exception, SLA credit, refund): not Support's to issue. Load team-handoff.
5. For (a), search_knowledge for what Support may do now: the Support charter (which accounts Support may credit at all), the credits-and-disputes page, and Finance's approval matrix for the per-line limit. The limit can depend on how the invoice was rated (e.g. which price book applies to the invoice's usage period): search the Finance close calendar for that, using the invoice period. Drafts, proposals and threads change nothing.
   - Support may credit this account and the copy line's full amount is within the limit: confirm_with_developer "I'll issue a credit note of $X (full amount) on the duplicated line L of invoice I." Only after yes: issue_credit_note (reason duplicate, memo with request ids). Tell them the credit note id and amount, and when it applies if the page says. No handoff.
   - Over the limit, or an account Support may not credit (e.g. contract/enterprise per the charter): do not credit or split. confirm_with_developer "I'll open a dispute on line L of invoice I (duplicate charge, request ids R) and hand it to Billing Ops." After yes: open_dispute, then load team-handoff and escalate with the dispute id.
   - If the developer says no: write nothing (no credit, dispute or case); say nothing was changed and they can come back.
6. For (b) and unexplained (c): gather intake (invoice, both lines, window in the account's billing timezone, request ids, what they checked) with ask_developer, then load team-handoff.
7. Never promise a dispute outcome or date. If a write is rejected, read get_invoice to see the state before saying anything."}

FP&A reviews any request as goodwill |"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/hosted-api-packages-free-tier-and-overage-policy.json", "chunk": "10/16", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Hosted API Packages: Free Tier, Included Usage, and Overage Policy", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-26", "text": "### Customer notifications

## Credits, refunds, and disputes (packaging interaction)
### Credits application order
Unless an order form specifies otherwise:
1) Included usage
2) Promotional or sales-issued credits
3) Overage charges
### Refunds/credits policy (high level)
- Billing disputes are governed by the dispute window in the MSA/order form.

---"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/discounting-and-credits-policy-for-usage-based-products.json", "chunk": "14/20", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Discounting and Credits Policy for Usage-Based Products", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-22", "text": "## Approval matrix (discounts and credits)
Approvals are required **before** sending a quote/Order Form, and before issuing credits that affect an invoice (unless covered by pre-approved support remediation bands).
Table: Approval requirements (minimum)
| Change type | Threshold (USD impact) | Who can approve | Required documentation |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Unit price discount (standard band) | <= $25k ARR equivalent or <= 10% effective discount | CRO (Jordan Blake) + Finance delegate (FP&A) | Deal record + pricing rationale |
| Unit price discount (non-standard) | > 10% or impacts gross margin model | CFO (Laura Bennett) + CRO | Deal record + margin impact summary |
| Promotional/trial credits | <= $10k total per account per quarter | CRO or CPO delegate + Finance delegate | Deal record + campaign/justification |
| Promotional/trial credits | > $10k per quarter | CFO + CRO | Written justification + expected conversion plan |
| Service credits (billing dispute / SLA) | <= $5k per invoice | Support manager + Finance (RevRec) | Support ticket + incident/billing evidence |"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/discounting-and-credits-policy-for-usage-based-products.json", "chunk": "10/20", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Discounting and Credits Policy for Usage-Based Products", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-22", "text": "## Dedicated usage: credits and discounts
- Discounts for Dedicated should generally be expressed as changes to **commit level** or **unit price for burst usage** (if burst is enabled).
- Credits may be applied to burst usage invoices or as an invoice-level service credit.
- Credits should not be used to effectively reduce a committed minimum without Finance approval; that changes contract economics and RevRec.
## Stacking rules
- Default: **one commercial discount** (unit price override or percent discount) may be active per meter at a time.
- Promotional credits may coexist with negotiated unit pricing.
- Additional stacking (e.g., unit price override + invoice percent discount + marketing credits) requires an exception approval."}, {"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance/billing-adjustments-approval-matrix.json", "chunk": "2/7", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix", "status": "final", "date": "2027-02-26", "text": "## Scope
- Direct Redwood invoices for Hosted API, Embeddings, Batch and Dedicated.
- Marketplace purchases are out of scope: adjustments go through the marketplace (see the marketplace invoicing notes).
- Contracted Enterprise accounts follow this matrix unless their order form names a different approver.
## Definitions
- **Adjustment**: any change to what a customer owes after an invoice is issued: a credit note, a refund, a write-off or a re-issued invoice.
- **Per line**: the amount of one invoice line, taken whole. An adjustment is never split across several smaller ones to stay under a limit.
- **Billing error**: a line that bills the wrong rate, quantity or product, or bills the same usage twice.
- **Goodwill**: any reduction of a correct charge, for any reason."}, {"source": "sources/slack/support/1749139920-goodwill-credit-asks-routing-finance.json", "chunk": "1/1", "kind": "Slack thread", "title": "#support thread 1749139920-goodwill-credit-asks-routing-finance", "status": "n/a", "date": "2025-06-05", "text": "channel: support
messages: Priya Shah: quick one - self-serve customer asking for a goodwill credit after the us-east blip yesterday. now that billing ops is live, do these go to billing ops?
Dev Patel: pretty sure no but want FP&A to confirm before it goes in the routing page. @Rishi Malhotra
Rishi Malhotra: correct, not billing ops. credit, goodwill and exception approvals come to Finance. open the case to finance with the ask, the amount if they gave one, and why. we decide. billing ops only applies what we approve
Rishi Malhotra: and please don't route these straight to legal. we pull legal in ourselves if it's non-standard comp or touches contract terms
Rachel Kim: +1. one carve-out: if the customer is asking what their contract or SLA actually says (terms, SLA %, what's covered), that's the account team - their CSM/TAM. not finance and not sales
Dev Patel: :thumbsup: thanks both, folding this into the routing page. the RACI draft is dead
Priya Shah: :pray: sending the goodwill ask to finance then"}, {"source": "sources/gmail/jasmine_liu/20261104-throughput-stitch-and-invoice-mitigation.json", "chunk": "3/8", "kind": "email thread", "title": "Throughput stitch & invoice mitigation plan for Friday spike", "status": "n/a", "date": "2026-11-04", "text": "1) Instant burst top-up (recommended for immediate protection): we add +3x capacity on your existing routes for 24 hours. This is billed as PAYG at our overrun rate; we can prorate to the hour. ETA: ~15 minutes to apply.
2) Temporary uplift with invoice smoothing: we apply the capacity now and massage the overrun across this month’s invoice so the spike is spread (no change to unit pricing). This requires a quick procurement acknowledgement from Ethan but we can do same day.
3) Partial courtesy credit (exception): I can request a one-time goodwill credit to offset up to 20% of the overage if approved by Sales Leadership and Finance. This is discretionary and tied to a short write-up you mentioned (postmortem).
If you’re interested in a longer-term fix, we can propose a short-term committed uplift (30–90 days) at a blended rate that will lower per-token cost vs PAYG for this window. If you’d like to discuss conversion to a reserved increment, we can model that."}]}

{"query": "March 2027 usage invoice price book billing period 2027 Close Calendar", "results": [{"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance/2027-close-calendar-and-invoice-periods.json", "chunk": "2/4", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods", "status": "final", "date": "2027-02-22", "text": "(continued) ## Monthly close calendar
Contracted accounts invoiced in arrears follow the same calendar; prepaid commitments are drawn down on BD2.
## Invoice periods and billing timezones
Until February 2027 every invoice period ran on UTC. From March 2027 usage onward, an account's invoice period runs from midnight to midnight in the account's billing timezone (`billing_timezone` on the account record; UTC unless set). A request belongs to the billing month, and to the invoice line, in which its timestamp falls in that timezone. For an account on America/Los_Angeles, a request at 03:00 UTC on 1 April 2027 is 20:00 on 31 March local time, so it is March usage and is billed on the March invoice.
Anything that reports a month of usage uses the same rule: the monthly total on the Console usage page, the invoice, and the figure Support gives a customer for a month. Usage before March 2027 stays on UTC periods and is not re-cut."}, {"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance/2027-close-calendar-and-invoice-periods.json", "chunk": "3/4", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods", "status": "final", "date": "2027-02-22", "text": "## Late usage
Usage that reaches the warehouse after BD1 is not added to an issued invoice. It is billed on the next month's invoice as a separate line marked "prior-period usage" with the original dates, so a customer comparing a month's export to its invoice may see those requests a month later.
## Price changes
A price-book change applies to usage from the first period that starts on or after its effective date. Mid-period changes are not prorated unless the order form says so.
The 2027 price book takes effect for usage from 1 March 2027: February 2027 and earlier usage is rated on the 2026 price book, and March 2027 usage onward on the 2027 price book."}, {"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance/2027-price-book-rollout-plan.json", "chunk": "1/1", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "2027 price book rollout plan (DRAFT)", "status": "draft", "date": "2026-12-15", "text": "title: 2027 price book rollout plan (DRAFT)

- Do we need 30 days' notice for self-serve? Legal to confirm.
- Should the effective date line up with the billing timezone change instead?
Next step: FP&A decision in January; the final date goes in the close calendar."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/support-console-record-format-changes-2027.json", "chunk": "3/5", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Console: Record Format Changes (April 2027)", "status": "published", "date": "2027-03-29", "text": "## Account field on writes
- On the writable tables (`cases`, `credit_notes`, `disputes`) the account field is now `billing_account_id`, on reads and writes. Its value is the account's `account_id`.
- A write or query on those tables that still sends `account_id` fails with an unknown-field error. Read-only tables keep `account_id`.
## Billing timezone
- Accounts have a `billing_timezone` (an IANA name such as `America/Los_Angeles`; `UTC` unless set).
- Which billing month and invoice line a request belongs to is set by Finance's invoice period rules; see Finance's 2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods (Finance shared drive)."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/batch-api-pricing-2027.json", "chunk": "1/1", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Batch API Pricing (2027)", "status": "published", "date": "2027-01-20", "text": "title: Batch API Pricing (2027)

body: ## Pricing
Batch API jobs are billed at 50% of the Hosted API per-token rate for the same model, with a completion window of 24 hours.
## How it shows on an invoice
Batch usage is billed on its own invoice lines, one per week, described as "Batch jobs, <start>-<end>". Each line links to the jobs it bills.
## Limits
- Up to 50,000 requests per job.
- Jobs that don't finish in 24 hours are cancelled; finished requests in a cancelled job are billed, unfinished ones are not.
_Last reviewed 2027-01-20._"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/finance-and-legal/billing-controls/collections-and-dunning-schedule-2027.json", "chunk": "1/1", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Collections: Dunning Schedule for Overdue Invoices (2027)", "status": "published", "date": "2027-01-15", "text": "title: Collections: Dunning Schedule for Overdue Invoices (2027)

body: ## Scope
Invoices still unpaid after their due date, once any automatic payment retries have finished. Payments that fail during a payment-processor incident are retried automatically and are not overdue; this page doesn't apply to them.
## Schedule
| Days past due | Step |
|---|---|
| 3 | Reminder email to the billing contact |
| 10 | Second reminder; account team copied |
| 21 | Final notice |
| 45 | Hosted API access suspended until paid |
## Changes from 2026
From 1 January 2027 the final notice is sent on day 21 instead of day 30.

If a current page says Support answers this without a case (an explanation, a general rule, a self-service step, "your account team confirms your terms", a known delay or threshold not yet reached, a failure inside a published incident window), answer and stop.
2. Pick the owning team from the current routing/approval/charter documents, not from drafts, proposals or chat threads. Use the console account (plan, channel, contracts) to choose between rows, e.g. self-serve vs signed contract, direct vs marketplace. If the developer claims something the console doesn't show (a contract, a plan), route per the policy for that situation.
3. Collect the intake the receiving team needs (the routing page lists it per row) with one ask_developer call: e.g. invoice_id, line_items, amounts, request_ids, time_of_issue together with timezone, error_code, checks_done, contract. Give windows in the account's billing_timezone (convert from what the developer said). If they don't have something, hand off anyway and record it as "not provided".
4. Do any permitted credit or dispute first (each needs the developer's explicit yes), because escalation closes the console. A plain handoff needs no confirmation.
5. escalate_case with: team; priority as the current pages say (normal for billing handoffs unless the routing page says urgent); summary (what they asked, what the console shows, what the team must decide/do); details with every fact given (ids, amounts as the console shows them, window in billing timezone, request ids, amount requested if any, what's missing); dispute_id if any. Never card numbers; if one was shared, write "customer shared a card number (removed)".
6. Tell the developer: anything the policy row says to tell the customer (e.g. a rule for their plan or channel), which team has it, the case id, and what that team will do next. No promised outcome, amount or date; no internal credit tables or ranges."}
